crops.name: Potatoes — ware (maincrop)
crops.overview: Rooster, Kerr's Pink and Golden Wonder are classic Irish varieties.
crops.ireland: Late blight pressure is high; most crops need a full protectant programme.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.0–6.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: FYM/compost in winter or before planting, after a clover ley. Permitted potassium sulphate (natural origin) where K index low.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.0–6.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Needs ~350–500 mm in season. Many Irish growers irrigate earlies/salads on light soils.
water.critical: Tuber initiation (from ~2–3 weeks after emergence) — scab control needs moist soil then; bulking stage for yield.

harvest.signs: Skins set (do not rub off), haulm dead 2–3 weeks
harvest.storage: Cure 10–14 days at 12–15°C, then store dark at 3–5°C (ware) or 2–4°C (seed); sprout suppressants only as permitted.

conventional.pests: Late blight (Phytophthora) is the main threat in Irish summers: protectant spray programme on a 5–10 day interval, using blight warnings (Met Éireann). Also aphids/virus (seed), blackleg, common scab, PCN, slugs, wireworm.

organic.pests: Blight-resistant varieties (e.g. Sárpo Mira, Carolus, Alouette), early planting of chitted seed, wider spacing, remove volunteers. Copper is restricted under EU organic rules (max 28 kg/ha over 7 years, ≈4 kg/ha/yr) and may not be allowed by your body — check first.
organic.weeds: Ridging and re-ridging, inter-row cultivation, flame weeding before emergence.

crops.rotation: 1 in 5 years or wider (PCN, blight volunteers, scab).

crops.name: Potatoes — seed
crops.overview: Grown under DAFM inspection; aphid and virus control are critical.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

planting.seed_rate: Certified seed only (DAFM Seed Potato Certification)

conventional.N: 100–140 kg N/ha (lower for small seed size)
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.0–6.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).

water.critical: Tuber initiation (from ~2–3 weeks after emergence) — scab control needs moist soil then; bulking stage for yield.

harvest.timing: Burn down early (July–Aug) to limit size and aphid-virus
harvest.signs: Tubers at seed size; aphid-flight burn-down dates
harvest.storage: Cure 10–14 days at 12–15°C, then store dark at 3–5°C (ware) or 2–4°C (seed); sprout suppressants only as permitted.

organic.weeds: Ridging and re-ridging, inter-row cultivation, flame weeding before emergence.

crops.name: Sugar beet
crops.ireland: Irish sugar processing ended in 2006; now grown mainly as fodder or for AD/niche.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.5–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Slurry/FYM, salt (sodium) is beneficial; boron often needed (permitted borate products if deficiency shown).
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.5–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Rain-fed; deep roots cope with dry spells.

harvest.storage: Clamp in a dry, frost-protected heap; feed by March.

conventional.pests: Aphids/virus yellows, beet cyst nematode, cercospora, powdery mildew, slugs; bolting from early sowing.
conventional.weeds: Low-dose herbicide programme (several passes) from pre-emergence.

organic.pests: Rotation, resistant varieties, sow when soil >7°C to reduce bolting, encourage beneficial insects.
organic.weeds: Very weed-sensitive: precision hoeing, finger weeders, hand-weeding; false seedbeds.
